meta.name: Ischemic Stroke — Left MCA, Within Thrombolytic Window

patient.name: Carol Whitfield
patient.chiefComplaint: Sudden right-sided weakness and inability to speak

history.hpi: Husband reports his wife was gardening when she suddenly stopped mid-sentence, dropped her trowel, and could not lift her right arm. She has not spoken a clear word since. He immediately called 911; time from last seen normal to the call was about 15 minutes.
pastMedical: Atrial fibrillation not on anticoagulation (patient-reported non-compliance)
history.lastOralIntake: Breakfast approximately 2 hours prior to onset
history.events: Husband witnessed sudden onset while gardening together; called 911 immediately

scene.dispatch: 66-year-old female, weakness, unable to speak, residence backyard
scene.location: Suburban home, back garden, patient seated on the ground where she was found
scene.safety: No hazards to crew noted, level ground
scene.bystanders: Husband present, witnessed onset directly, gives clear last-known-well time
visualCues: Patient seated on ground, right arm limp in her lap
Patient attempting to speak but producing only garbled sounds
Husband holding his phone, showing the exact time he called 911

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 66-year-old female with acute right-sided weakness, facial droop, and expressive aphasia witnessed by her husband approximately 15 minutes ago.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right-sided facial droop, right arm drift, unable to lift right arm against gravity, right leg weak
otherFindings: Expressive aphasia — understands commands but cannot form words
Husband confirms exact time of onset
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Uh... uh..." (unable to form words, clearly frustrated)

transitions.condition: Crew performs a validated stroke scale, confirms blood glucose is normal, establishes a precise last-known-well time from the husband, and places the patient on a cardiac monitor.

phases.name: Stroke scale performed, LKW established
phases.description: Crew completes a validated stroke scale confirming a positive finding, checks blood glucose to rule out a stroke mimic, and documents a precise last-known-well time within the thrombolytic window.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew performs a validated stroke scale (positive for facial droop, arm drift, and speech abnormality), checks blood glucose to exclude hypoglycemia as a mimic, and establishes last known well at 15 minutes prior to arrival.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right facial droop, right arm drift, right leg weak
otherFindings: Stroke scale positive for all three components
Blood glucose 132 mg/dL, not a mimic
Last known well documented at 15 minutes prior to EMS arrival
Cardiac monitor placed, showing atrial fibrillation

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform validated prehospital stroke scale (facial droop, arm drift, speech) — positive for all three
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use a validated prehospital stroke scale that may include, but is not limited to: Facial smile/grimace, Arm drift, Speech
expectedActions.rationale: A validated scale drives the transport and pre-notification decision.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a stroke mimic (result 132 mg/dL, no treatment needed)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check blood glucose level (BGL). Treat only if glucose less than 60 mg/dL
expectedActions.rationale: Hypoglycemia is a common, rapidly reversible stroke mimic.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish precise last-known-well time from husband (15 minutes prior to EMS arrival)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Determine "last known well" time. History – "last known well" and source of that information
expectedActions.rationale: LKW time determines thrombolytic and thrombectomy eligibility at the receiving hospital.

expectedActions.shortAction: Do not treat elevated blood pressure in the field
expectedActions.rationale: Permissive hypertension maintains cerebral perfusion pressure to the ischemic penumbra; lowering BP prehospital can worsen the stroke.

transitions.condition: The positive severity findings (dense hemiparesis plus aphasia) raise concern for a large vessel occlusion; crew provides early notification to a thrombectomy-capable stroke center and minimizes scene time.

transitions.if: Blood pressure treated in the field
transitions.condition: Crew becomes concerned about the elevated blood pressure and attempts to lower it, against protocol guidance not to treat hypertension in suspected stroke.

phases.name: LVO suspected, thrombectomy center notified
phases.description: With a positive severity scale suggesting possible large vessel occlusion, the crew minimizes scene time, avoids treating the elevated blood pressure, and transports directly to a thrombectomy-capable stroke center with early notification.
phases.triggerCondition: Given the dense hemiparesis and aphasia within the thrombolytic window, the crew treats this as a possible LVO, bypasses lower-tier facilities per the local stroke plan, and gives early notification to allow the stroke team to prepare.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right facial droop, right arm drift, right leg weak, unchanged
otherFindings: Head of stretcher elevated 15-30 degrees, neck neutral
Thrombectomy-capable center notified with LKW time and scale findings

expectedActions.shortAction: Elevate head of stretcher 15-30 degrees with neck neutral; protect the weak right arm
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Prevent aspiration – elevate head of stretcher 15–30 degrees if systolic BP greater than 100 mmHg. Maintain head and neck in neutral alignment, without flexing the neck. Protect paralyzed limbs from injury
expectedActions.rationale: Reduces aspiration risk and prevents injury to the flaccid limb during transport.

expectedActions.shortAction: Notify thrombectomy-capable stroke center early with LKW time and positive severity scale findings
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Positive stroke severity scale with time of onset or last known well less than 24 hours may be eligible for mechanical thrombectomy — Consider transport to hospital capable of mechanical thrombectomy per local stroke plan. Early hospital notification per local stroke plan that should include any suspected large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke
expectedActions.rationale: Early notification of a possible LVO allows the receiving center to mobilize the stroke and interventional team before arrival.

phases.name: Blood pressure treated in the field
phases.description: The crew attempts to lower the patient's elevated blood pressure out of concern for stroke severity, contrary to protocol. This risks dropping cerebral perfusion pressure to the ischemic penumbra and worsening the neurologic deficit.
phases.triggerCondition: Concerned by the systolic blood pressure in the 180s, the crew administers or considers an antihypertensive agent, which is explicitly against the stroke protocol's guidance.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right facial droop and arm weakness appear slightly more pronounced
otherFindings: Blood pressure dropping after inappropriate treatment attempt
Deficit not improving, possibly subtly worsening

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize inappropriate BP treatment; resume permissive hypertension and expedite transport
expectedActions.rationale: Once recognized, the crew should stop further BP-lowering efforts and expedite transport to limit further penumbra compromise.
